name: Recursive Teaching Dimension of the Chen Neighbor Puncture
proof: The full-domain removal plan in sync/chen_neighbor_puncture_certificate.json.gz is a recursive teaching plan of width at most four. Its checker compares the actual remaining words at every removal and verifies that the recorded sample uniquely identifies the removed word. For the lower bound, direct enumeration of all 220 three-coordinate sets shows that every realized trace has at least two realizers in the original 109-word class. Thus no target has a teaching set of size three or less: a smaller teaching set could be padded to size three. No width-three recursive plan can make its first removal, so RTD is at least four. This ordinary-RTD lower bound is separate from the shattered-set argument used for VC and projected RTD.
references: Definition-driven certificate and independent replay: sync/verify_chen_neighbor_puncture.py; sync/chen_neighbor_puncture_certificate.json.gz. The original Chen base is from \cite{chen2016recursive}; the puncture modification and its separation proof are local results.
